Accepted papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series, possibly also in the WIDER Working Paper Series, and carry a one-off research honorarium of US$3,000-10,000 paid on delivery.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a research commissioning call, not a degree scholarship: a team delivers a policy-ready working paper on South African tax, revenue and labour-market questions built primarily on the country's administrative tax data, and is paid a one-off honorarium only when the deliverable is accepted. Because that honorarium is explicitly expected to absorb every research cost - data work, research assistance, writing time - applicants should scope a project that fits comfortably inside the US$3,000-10,000 band rather than budgeting as if more support will follow. Payment is conditional on acceptance, and copyright transfers to UNU-WIDER under a consultant or institutional contract, so anyone who must retain publishing rights should weigh that before applying.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Economics researchers - especially early-career, female, South Africa-based or Global South scholars, and teams involving Historically Disadvantaged Institutions - who can work with anonymized South African tax administrative data and produce a policy-relevant paper.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the proposal answers a listed WS2 or WS3 topic and that South African tax administrative data sits at the core of the design, not at the edge
Download the official proposal form template and cover page and build the proposal inside them from the start
Trim every CV to five pages or less and collect address, gender, nationality and date of birth for each researcher before opening the online form
Open the correct online form (individual / group / non-profit organization) early and rehearse the uploads well before the final day
Read the published queries and responses on the announcement page before assuming anything about data access, eligibility or formatting
common_rejection_risks: Proposal drifts outside the two workstreams or only marginally uses South African tax administrative data
Feasibility doubts about reaching and cleaning confidential National Treasury data in time for the 8 June 2027 draft
Team credentials that do not support the honorarium tier - the lead researcher's qualifications drive the amount
Wrong online form, missing co-researcher details, or over-length CVs and papers that fail the initial screen
Ignoring the provided template or skipping required uploads, which can sink an otherwise strong idea
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Beyond the one-off honorarium and the small non-Gauteng travel stipend, applicants fund everything themselves: the honorarium is published as covering all research expenses, so data collection, research assistance and any further travel or conference participation must be planned within the award.
document_audit: Every researcher's CV must be five pages or less - there is no senior-academic exception
The proposal must follow the provided template, include the cover page, and stay within 10,000 words counting tables, figures, footnotes and references
Personal details (address, gender, nationality, date of birth) of all researchers must be entered on the online form, not just the lead applicant's
No budget is required - submitting one adds no value and can distract the screen
Teams needing National Treasury tax data should line up confidentiality agreements early, since the first draft is due 8 June 2027

Payment comes only after the deliverable is deemed acceptable, and copyright transfers to UNU-WIDER on signing the contract (it can revert if no further publication is expected)
Researchers outside Gauteng using the tax data can request the small travel stipend; those inside Gauteng cannot
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Prepare the template-based proposal and cover page, open the matching online form for individuals, groups or NGOs linked from the announcement page, enter every researcher's details, upload the documents, and submit before the hard 23:59 (UTC+2) cutoff on 15 October 2026.
